limits: No global quiescence or thread-safety guarantee follows from a Stop name. Some waits are ignored; TerminateThread results are ignored; derived event objects are destroyed before the base thread join. A failed module finalize can also null its interface fields without deleting still-live objects.
This contract does not transfer lifetime of an externally freed buffer, make shallow CDatMonBuffer copies safe, or prove external callbacks cannot invalidate caller state.

CreateDrs changes the retained ring serial mode only after successful synchronous Run57. The setter returns the old mode and does not acquire a lock.

wrapper_cleanup: DMInterface stores its backend pointer at+4. Its destructor calls backend.DeleteDMInterface; it does not delete the caller buffer. Legacy/dual use backend vtable2C; phase5/phase6 use18. The engine later deletes backend and wrapper objects separately.

Legacy/phase5/phase6 DiagInterface.DeleteDMInterface signals stop and waits15000ms for its idle event. The wait result is ignored. With writer nonnull it calls writer.WriteTable(DeleteDmInterfaceSnd) and clears callback pointer+3C. With no DLL and no writer it only invalidates ready; a missing DLL entry can skip callback clearing.
J2534 legacy/phase5/phase6 DeleteDMInterface overrides only clear callback+3C. dualdiag base DeleteDMInterface is an actual no-op. These are not caller-buffer deallocators.

Legacy/phase5/phase6 backend destructors reset run, signal exit/stop, wait10000ms and call TerminateThread after any nonzero wait result. They then close their events/thread handle and critical section, free each12-byte registration node through a direct free wrapper, and unload a nonnull DLL. They do not free node.buffer.

J2534 derived destructors delete owned queue/event objects before the base destructor joins its thread. Event destructors free their own payload/assembly/routine allocations. Their borrowed normal buffer fields remain untouched. Active-event destruction composes the separately owned Actuation contracts.
Dual backend destruction closes its own events/thread/critical section and frees only its registration nodes. Its nested owned event objects do not transfer ownership of normal buffers.

writer_path.constructor: For DiagInterface ctor(param1==1,writer), writer is borrowed at legacy+44 or phase5/phase6+40. DLL+4 is initialized0. LoadLibraryW(ComTol32.dll) occurs only when writer is null. A nonnull writer therefore bypasses that provider in these actual recorded interfaces; no ownership of the writer is taken.
writer_path.deletion: With writer nonnull, DeleteDMInterface writes a command row through writer.vtable14. The final backend destructor writes DeleteDiagInterfaceSnd through the same slot. These are recorded commands, not calls into ComTol32. DeleteDiagInterfaceSnd has no payload and does not carry the caller buffer.
writer_path.post_stop: The selected native wrapper/event/backend destructors do not own or free the caller CDatMonBuffer or its embedded ring/signal allocations. They drop borrowed registrations and free their own storage. This preserves caller ownership, not buffer contents: normal Stop/acquisition can update recorded state, and those algorithms remain separate contracts. Continued use requires a valid externally owned allocation and the explicit concurrency/error limits below.
